extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, securities lawyers, compliance officers, investors, and commenters on SEC rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and implementation guidance for the SEC's final rules on climate-related disclosures (Regulation S-K subpart 1500 and Article 14 of Regulation S-X), including alternatives considered, burdens, assurance, tagging, materiality thresholds, and PRA burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize reporting to improve comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: By standardizing reporting practices, the final rules would level the playing field among firms, making it easier for investors to assess registrants' climate-related risks against competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization enables peer benchmarking, contributes to increased competition for capital, and helps investors compare registrants across and within industries. The Commission emphasizes consistency and comparability as primary benefits that justify some prescriptive elements of the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit managerial attention to material climate risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules should elicit disclosures primarily for registrants for which climate-related risks have materially impacted or are reasonably likely to materially impact financials or business strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits managerial burdens in settings where climate issues are not material. The rules include materiality qualifiers and less prescriptive requirements to avoid imposing significant managerial attention where unwarranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit ISO 14064-3 attestation standard for GHG assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will permit assurance providers to use the ISO 14064-3 attestation standard for GHG emissions assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing ISO 14064-3 should limit circumstances requiring registrants to seek different attestation engagements and mitigate costs associated with obtaining assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in periods for GHG emissions disclosure and assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended phase-in periods are provided for compliance with GHG emissions disclosure and assurance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase-in periods give registrants time to seek assurance providers, allow markets to respond to increased demand for services, and give non-accountant attestation providers time to adapt to independence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate Scope 3 requirement (to reduce burden/competitive risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules eliminate the proposed requirement to disclose Scope 3 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing Scope 3 reporting reduces compliance costs and helps limit circumstances in which disclosure of potentially competitive business information would be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow Regulation S-X requirements and include materiality qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules significantly narrow the Regulation S-X requirements and add materiality qualifiers and less prescriptive disclosure requirements for subpart 1500 of Regulation S-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes are intended to limit scope, reduce burdens, and focus disclosure on information material to investors, mitigating disclosure of proprietary or competitively sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude private targets in business combinations from disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules no longer apply disclosure requirements to a private company that is a party to a business combination transaction (S-4/F-4 registered offerings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mitigates competitive disadvantages in acquisition contexts where public acquirers would otherwise need to screen targets for ability to produce required disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt SRCs and EGCs from GHG emissions disclosures and provide longer phase-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Small reporting companies (SRCs) and emerging growth companies (EGCs) are not required to provide GHG emissions disclosures and are given longer phase-in periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acknowledges disproportionate fixed costs on smaller registrants and allows them to observe other registrants' practices before reporting, lowering implementation burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures should reduce information asymmetry to aid capital formation
rubrics_metrics.description: More consistent, comparable, and reliable disclosures could reduce information asymmetries between managers and investors, improving liquidity and lowering costs of capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced asymmetry may improve investors' cash flow estimates, narrow bid-ask spreads, mitigate adverse selection, and attract more investors—benefits weighed against compliance costs when assessing rule design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider investor preference shifts and non-diversifiable climate risk effects on cost of capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures can change investor demand depending on preferences and may reveal non-diversifiable climate-related risk that commands a risk premium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission recognizes that disclosures could increase or decrease a registrant’s cost of capital if investors update expectations about exposure to non-diversifiable climate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh potential for market exit/avoidance against benefits of public registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether compliance costs could lead marginal companies to avoid or exit public markets, and balance that against the benefits of being public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some commenters raised avoidance concerns, the Commission concluded public-market benefits (liquidity, lower cost of capital) make widespread avoidance unlikely; modifications and phase-ins mitigate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles-based vs prescriptive disclosure approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider a more principles-based approach (registrant chooses what to disclose) versus a prescriptive approach (detailed required metrics and formats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles-based can reduce reporting costs and boilerplate but may reduce comparability, increase shareholder confusion, and permit cherry-picking favorable measures/time horizons. Prescriptive improves comparability and reduces boilerplate but can increase compliance costs. The final rules take a mixed approach: prescriptive elements retained where needed for comparability, with materiality qualifiers and less prescriptive elements in other areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives for assurance over GHG emissions (none/limited/reasonable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered alternatives: no assurance requirement; reasonable assurance for all GHG disclosures; or requiring reasonable assurance only for LAFs (Large Accelerated Filers) or similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher assurance increases reliability but also costs. The final rules limit the scope of required assurance (e.g., LAFs) to balance reliability with compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance provider independence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require GHG emissions assurance providers to be independent with respect to the registrant and its affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An independence requirement provides investor confidence that attestations are objective; however, it may increase costs or reduce available providers. The rule mitigates these impacts via phase-in periods to allow market and provider adjustments or unwinding conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bright-line quantitative thresholds versus principles-based materiality for financial statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered using a principles-based materiality approach versus bright-line quantitative thresholds for Regulation S-X financial statement disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bright-line quantitative thresholds provide regulatory certainty, predictable application, reduce underreporting risk, and increase comparability across registrants. De minimis exceptions are included to avoid anomalous triggers for smaller or atypical registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include de minimis exceptions to avoid anomalous triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt de minimis thresholds so disclosures are not triggered in anomalous situations where balance-sheet items do not scale with operations (e.g., highly leveraged or loss-making firms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De minimis thresholds reduce overly granular, non-decision-useful disclosure that could arise from strict bright-line rules in anomalous financial situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not limit Regulation S-X disclosures to certain sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of restricting new Regulation S-X disclosures to registrants in certain sectors was rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sector limitations would reduce information for other sectors affected by climate events and risk becoming obsolete as conditions change; broad application preserves future relevance and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require climate disclosures to be filed (not furnished) to preserve investor remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules require registrants to file (rather than furnish) climate-related disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing allows investors to bring suit (e.g., Exchange Act section 18), improves avenues for redress, and promotes accuracy and consistency because registrants face securities-law liabilities for filed statements. Furnishing would lower liability but could limit investor benefit and accuracy incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat certain forward-looking subpart 1500 disclosures as PSLRA forward-looking statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt provision stating that disclosures (other than historic facts) under certain new subpart 1500 provisions constitute 'forward-looking statements' for PSLRA safe harbor purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces litigation risk for registrants making forward-looking climate statements and is part of mitigations to address concerns about filing rather than furnishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider (but generally reject) complete exemption of SRCs/EGCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered fully exempting SRCs and EGCs from the final rules but rejected because it would leave significant information gaps and detract from comparability and informational benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, the rules reduce prescriptiveness, provide phase-in periods, and exempt SRCs/EGCs specifically from GHG emissions disclosure to mitigate burden while preserving core information for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit substituted compliance/home-country disclosure frameworks (not adopted now)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider allowing registrants to comply by using disclosures provided under other jurisdictions' frameworks (substituted compliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although substituted compliance could reduce costs if requirements overlap, the Commission determined it is premature given development status of international frameworks and will monitor developments before deciding on accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept GHG data solely from other regulatory regimes (e.g., GHGRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered requiring registrants to submit GHG data they report under other regulatory regimes instead of SEC-specific disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports for other regimes serve different purposes and are not always presented in ways that are decision-useful to investors; therefore, the Commission declined this alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline XBRL tagging scope should be broad to enable machine-readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered narrowing Inline XBRL tagging (e.g., excluding climate-related disclosures or tagging only quantitative items) but concluded such narrowing would provide only modest cost savings and would reduce investor benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad tagging facilitates extraction, comparison, redlining across periods, and machine analyses (tonality, sentiment, risk-word detection) of narrative climate-related disclosures. Narrower tagging could force manual searches and hinder automated processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) collection requirements and affected forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain provisions create 'collection of information' requirements under the PRA affecting Forms S-1, F-1, S-4, F-4, S-11, 10, 20-F, and 10-K; collections require valid OMB control numbers and responses are mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Climate-related disclosures under subpart 1500 and Article 14 must be included in registration statements and annual reports; Article 14 disclosures belong in a note to the financial statements. The GHG emissions disclosure and related attestation burden are attributed to the Form 10-K for PRA purposes even if incorporated from a Form 10-Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update outside professional cost rate to $600/hour for burden estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission updated the OMB inventory professional cost burden estimate from $400/hr to $600/hr to adjust for inflation dating from Aug. 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This update affects PRA burden cost totals across affected collections (PRA Table 1) and is used solely to present updated current inventory numbers; it is not a new burden imposed by the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard burden allocation between internal hours and outside professional costs
rubrics_metrics.description: For PRA burden estimates, apply standard percentage allocations of internal vs outside professional burden: Forms S-1, F-1, S-4, F-4, S-11, 10, and 20-F = 25% internal / 75% outside; Form 10-K = 75% internal / 25% outside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these percentages (PRA Table 2) to allocate cost estimates when deriving total burden hours and costs for each affected collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate targets from metrics and use 'financial statement disclosures' terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: When estimating burdens, separate disclosures related to targets from metrics, and replace 'financial statement metrics' with 'financial statement disclosures' because the final rules do not describe such items as 'metrics'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change better reflects the content and nature of the Regulation S-X amendments and informs the structure of PRA burden calculations and categorization of disclosure sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use external sources (UK BEIS/FCA) and commenters' input for cost estimates, erring conservatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Paperwork burden and direct cost estimates rely in part on the UK's BEIS impact assessment, FCA cost-benefit analysis, and cost estimates provided by commenters; estimates are conservative (likely an upper bound).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes these inputs provide a reasonable means to estimate collection burdens but may overstate costs to avoid understating compliance impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate multi-year average PRA burden over nine years
rubrics_metrics.description: Because one amendment's requirement phases in as late as the ninth year, the Commission estimated a nine-year average PRA burden rather than the typical three-year average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden estimates account for variability across registrants (size, complexity, existing disclosures, other jurisdictions) and allocate burden between internal hours and outside professional costs using the stated conversion rates and allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert outside professional costs to internal burden hours using $441/hour conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: To derive estimated total burden hours, the Commission converts outside professional cost estimates into internal burden hours using a conversion rate of $441/hr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conversion is applied after allocating cost estimates between internal and external portions per PRA Table 2 when producing PRA Table 3 total burden hour estimates.
